text: Now Moses was keeping the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, priest of Midian; he led the flock far out into the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
There the angel of the LORD appeared to him as flames of fire coming out of a bush; Moses looked, and though the bush was blazing, it was not burning up.
So Moses thought, I will go over and look at this strange sight — why the bush isn't burning away.
When the LORD saw that he had turned aside to look, God called out to him from inside the bush, Moses! Moses! And he answered, Here I am.
God said, do not come any closer; take your sandals off your feet, because the ground you are standing on is holy.
Then he said, I am the God of your father — the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. At that Moses covered his face, afraid to look at God.
The LORD said, I have plainly seen the misery of my people in Egypt, and I have heard them crying out because of their slave drivers; I know well what they are suffering.

So I have come down to rescue them from the power of Egypt and to bring them up out of that land into a good, wide land, a land flowing with milk and honey — the territory of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
And now the cry of the Israelites has reached me, and I have also seen how harshly the Egyptians are treating them.
So come now, I am sending you to Pharaoh, to bring my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt.
But Moses said to God, who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?
God answered, I will be with you; and this will be your sign that I am the one who sent you: after you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will worship God on this very mountain.
Moses said to God, suppose I go to the Israelites and tell them, the God of your fathers has sent me to you, and they ask me, what is his name — what shall I tell them?
God said to Moses, I AM WHO I AM. This is what you are to tell the Israelites: I AM has sent me to you.

God also told Moses, say this to the Israelites: the LORD, the God of your fathers — the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob — has sent me to you. This is my name forever, the name to be remembered from generation to generation.

Go and gather the elders of Israel together and tell them, the LORD, the God of your fathers, appeared to me — the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — and said, I have watched over you and have seen what is being done to you in Egypt.
And I have promised to bring you up out of your suffering in Egypt into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey.

The elders will listen to you. Then you, together with the elders, are to go to the king of Egypt and say to him, the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us; now let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to the LORD our God.
But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless he is forced by a mighty hand.
So I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all the wonders I am about to do there; after that, he will let you go.
And I will cause the Egyptians to view this people favorably, so that when you leave, you will not go away empty-handed.

Every woman is to ask her neighbor and any woman staying in her house for objects of silver and gold and for clothing, which you will put on your sons and daughters — in this way you will plunder the Egyptians.
